The snake plant, Dracaena trifasciata 'Laurentii', is the oldest plant in the house: a piece of Aunt Winifred's from her cottage at Widecombe-in-the-Moor, given to me in a margarine tub in 1998 when I started at the primary school. It sat on my classroom windowsill for twenty-two years and survived three Ofsted inspections, a flood in the art cupboard and Class 4 pouring orange squash into it in 2007. Divided it on 24 March 2024 into three with a bread knife: one stays on the landing, one went to Brenda Prowse, one to the village hall. Waters every six to eight weeks in winter, monthly in summer. Flowered once, in June 2016, a stalk of small cream flowers that smelled of honeysuckle at night.
